conflicts.permit: When you use some products, services, or post your comments, the personal information you share is visible to other users and can be read, collected, or used by them.
conflicts.prohibit: We DO NOT collect, store or use any personal information while you visit, download or upgrade our website or our products, excepting the personal information that you submit to us when you create a user account, send an error report.
conflicts.situation: A user posts a comment containing personal information through a product, which the company stores and displays to other users.
conflicts.reason: The exception covers only account creation and error reports; posted comments are not listed, and the policy does not say whether comment content falls under the exception.

conflicts.permit: When signing up as a subscriber to TED’s ad-free video content in TED’s iOS app, TED may collect your personal information to manage, store and process subscriber information, including your name, email address and if provided, your TED subscriber ID.
conflicts.prohibit: TED does not collect, process or store any personal information from subscribers of TED ad-free video content through the iOS app unless a user contacts TED directly via support.
conflicts.situation: A user signs up as an ad-free subscriber in the TED iOS app without contacting support; TED collects name and email.
conflicts.reason: Both statements address the same subscription in the same iOS app. The only exception, contacting support, does not cover sign-up, so collection and non-collection are both asserted.

conflicts.permit: We may collect non-personal information about the computer, mobile device or other device you use to access TED Sites, such as IP address, geolocation information, unique device identifiers, browser type, browser language and other preferences automatically collected.
conflicts.prohibit: but we don’t collect any geolocation-specific data from you or your device
conflicts.situation: A visitor uses TED Sites on a mobile device and TED automatically collects device data including geolocation information.
conflicts.reason: One section lists geolocation information collected from the device; the location section denies collecting any geolocation-specific data from the device. No condition separates the two.

conflicts.permit: We may collect non-personal information about the computer, mobile device or other device you use to access TED Sites, such as IP address, geolocation information, unique device identifiers, browser type, browser language and other preferences automatically collected.
conflicts.prohibit: We collect information about your location to provide you with the most localized experience possible, but never collect data from your device.
conflicts.situation: TED automatically collects geolocation information and device identifiers from the device a visitor uses to access TED Sites.
conflicts.reason: The summary says TED never collects data from the device, while the device data section describes automatic collection from the device. The policy gives no precedence or exception.

conflicts.permit: We may disclose Personal Data to our third party service providers to provide you with the Services, including our third party payment processor.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not sell, rent, or otherwise share your data to any third-party for a business or commercial purpose, other than the Auction House.
conflicts.situation: A Nevada resident buys an auction item and their name and billing address are shared with the third-party payment processor.
conflicts.reason: The Nevada statement excepts only the Auction House, but the general section shares Personal Data with service providers for a business purpose. The policy does not say which governs Nevada users.

conflicts.permit: We share Aggregate Information with companies that provide public relations and marketing services for us.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not sell, rent, or otherwise share your data to any third-party for a business or commercial purpose, other than the Auction House.
conflicts.situation: A Nevada resident's usage data, including device ID and location, is shared with a marketing services company.
conflicts.reason: Aggregate Information is collected about the user and shared with marketing firms, a commercial purpose; the Nevada statement excepts only the Auction House and does not exclude aggregate data.

conflicts.permit: The information collected through these means (including IP address) is disclosed to these service providers, who use the information to analyze use of our website.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not sell, rent, or otherwise share your data to any third-party for a business or commercial purpose, other than the Auction House.
conflicts.situation: A Nevada resident visits the website and their IP address is disclosed to Google Analytics.
conflicts.reason: Disclosure to analytics providers is a business purpose and is not covered by the Auction House exception. The policy does not reconcile the two statements.

conflicts.permit: Where you choose to do this, we will receive certain profile information about you from your social media provider.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not receive any information from third parties.
conflicts.situation: A user registers with a Facebook or Twitter account and the company receives profile information from the social media provider.
conflicts.reason: The summary flatly denies receiving any information from third parties, while the social login section says profile data is received from the provider. No exception is stated.

conflicts.permit: basic account information, including your name, email, gender, birthday, current city, and profile picture URL, as well as other information that you choose to make public.
conflicts.prohibit: We do not receive any information from third parties.
conflicts.situation: A user uses the Facebook application and the company accesses their Facebook basic account information by default.
conflicts.reason: Accessing Facebook account data by default is receipt of information from a third party, which the summary denies without exception.

conflicts.permit: basic account information, including your name, email, gender, birthday, current city, and profile picture URL, as well as other information that you choose to make public.
conflicts.situation: A California user uses the Facebook application and the company accesses their gender and birthday.
conflicts.reason: The CCPA table marks gender and date of birth as not collected in the past twelve months, while the Facebook section says they are accessed by default. The policy does not reconcile them.

conflicts.permit: We may request access or permission to track location-based information from your mobile device, either continuously or while you are using our mobile application(s), to provide certain location-based services.
conflicts.situation: A California user grants location permission to the app and the company tracks device location.
conflicts.reason: The CCPA table marks geolocation data (device location) as not collected, while other sections describe collecting device location. The time frame of the table does not clearly separate them.

conflicts.permit: We may share your information with certain Google Maps Platform APIs (e.g., Google Maps API, Places API).
conflicts.prohibit: MTP Holdings inc has not disclosed or sold any personal information to third parties for a business or commercial purpose in the preceding twelve (12) months.
conflicts.situation: A user's location information is shared with Google Maps Platform APIs to provide location-based services.
conflicts.reason: Sharing with Google is a disclosure to a third party for a business purpose, which the CCPA notice denies. The policy does not state an exception or date separating them.

conflicts.permit: We may disclose your personal information with our service providers pursuant to a written contract between us and each service provider.
conflicts.prohibit: MTP Holdings inc has not disclosed or sold any personal information to third parties for a business or commercial purpose in the preceding twelve (12) months.
conflicts.situation: The company discloses user personal information to a for-profit service provider processing data on its behalf.
conflicts.reason: Disclosure to service providers is typically a business-purpose disclosure; the policy does not say whether service providers are excluded from third parties in the denial.

conflicts.permit: However, we may retain some information in our files to prevent fraud, troubleshoot problems, assist with any investigations, enforce our legal terms and/or comply with applicable legal requirements.
conflicts.prohibit: No purpose in this notice will require us keeping your personal information for longer than the period of time in which users have an account with us.
conflicts.situation: A user terminates their account and the company keeps some information afterward to troubleshoot problems or prevent fraud.
conflicts.reason: The legal-requirement exception covers only part of the post-termination retention; troubleshooting and fraud prevention are not covered, and the policy does not say which statement governs.

conflicts.permit: We may process your information to develop and display personalized content and advertising tailored to your interests, location, and more.
conflicts.prohibit: Inferences drawn from any of the collected personal information listed above to create a profile or summary about, for example, an individual’s preferences and characteristics
conflicts.situation: The company infers a California user's interests from their activity to tailor advertising.
conflicts.reason: Targeted advertising implies inferring preferences, but the CCPA table marks inferences as not collected. Whether tailoring involves such inferences is vague.
